ai.literal: That which will be lost and, that which will be produced and, having become, afterwards will yield profit and, having considered, act.
ai.translation: Weigh what will be lost, what will be gained, and the ultimate profit that will result, before undertaking an action.
ai.modern: ஒரு செயலைத் தொடங்கும் முன், அதனால் அழியும் பொருளையும், ஆகும் பொருளையும், முடிவில் அது தரும் ஊதியத்தையும் ஆராய்ந்து செய்ய வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet advises careful calculation before starting any enterprise. The words 'aḻivatūum' and 'āvatūum' refer to the initial capital or effort expended and the immediate returns generated, both lengthened for musical emphasis. One must weigh these against the ultimate, long-term profit ('ūtiyam') that will result ('āki vaḻi payakkum'). Only after thoroughly considering all three factors should one proceed with the action.

ai.literal: To those who do having thought having considered with a selected group, rare thing whatever even one is not.
ai.translation: For those who deliberate thoroughly and act in the company of chosen associates, there is no achievement too difficult to attain.
ai.modern: தக்க அறிஞர்கள் கூட்டத்தோடு சேர்ந்து, ஒரு செயலை நன்கு ஆராய்ந்து திட்டமிட்டுச் செய்பவர்களுக்கு, செய்வதற்கு அரிய செயல் என்று எதுவும் இல்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the importance of careful planning and good counsel. The phrase 'terinta inattotu' refers to a well-chosen group of knowledgeable associates. When a person deliberates deeply with such a group before acting, no goal or achievement ('arumporul') remains out of reach.

ai.literal: Profit desiring, capital which loses undertaking, will not undertake the wise.
ai.translation: The wise will not undertake an action that risks the capital in the hope of making a profit.
ai.modern: லாபத்தை விரும்பி இருக்கும் முதலையும் இழக்கச் செய்யும் செயல்களை அறிவுடையவர்கள் தொடங்க மாட்டார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against reckless ventures. It states that wise people will not engage in actions that might destroy their initial capital just because they desire a potential profit. The word mutal refers to the base capital or existing resources, while aakkam denotes the expected gain. True wisdom lies in protecting what one already has before attempting to multiply it.

ai.literal: Clarity without that-which-is they-will-not-begin disgrace called affliction those-who-fear.
ai.translation: Those who fear the affliction called disgrace will not begin an action that lacks clarity.
ai.modern: இழிவு என்னும் துன்பத்திற்குப் பயப்படுகின்றவர்கள், தெளிவு இல்லாத எந்த ஒரு செயலையும் தொடங்க மாட்டார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against undertaking actions without a clear understanding of the methods and consequences. The word 'தெளிவு' refers to a clear, well-thought-out plan. Those who dread the sorrow and shame that come from failure will never start a poorly understood task. Thus, careful deliberation is the only shield against disgrace.

ai.literal: Details completely without considering rising, enemies garden bed establishing a way.
ai.translation: Setting out to act without exhaustively considering every detail is a way of planting one's enemies in a well-prepared bed.
ai.modern: எல்லா வகைகளையும் முழுமையாக ஆராயாமல் ஒரு செயலைத் தொடங்குவது, பகைவர்களைப் பாத்தி கட்டி வளர்ப்பதற்குச் சமமான ஒரு வழியாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against hasty action. The word 'vakai' refers to the various details or categories of an undertaking, and 'aṟa' means to exhaust them completely. If a leader rises to act without such thorough deliberation ('cūḻātu'), they inadvertently create the perfect conditions for their enemies to thrive. The poet uses the agricultural image of a 'pātti' (a prepared garden bed) to show how poor planning actively cultivates and strengthens one's opposition.

ai.literal: things fit to be done / things that are not / by doing / will be ruined / things fit to be done / not doing / also by / will be ruined
ai.translation: One will be ruined by doing what should not be done, and will also be ruined by not doing what should be done.
ai.modern: செய்யத்தகாத செயல்களைச் செய்வதால் ஒருவன் அழிவான்; செய்யத்தக்க செயல்களைச் செய்யாமல் விடுவதாலும் அவன் அழிவான்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against two paths to failure: wrong action and harmful inaction. The phrase 'செய்தக்க அல்ல செய' refers to committing acts that are unfit or inappropriate, which leads to ruin. Conversely, 'செய்தக்க செய்யாமை' points to the failure to perform necessary and proper actions, which is equally destructive. The repetition of 'கெடும்' (will be ruined) underscores the inevitable downfall that results from both errors in judgment.

ai.literal: Having considered, let one decide on an action; after having decided, saying 'we will consider' is a flaw.
ai.translation: Consider carefully before deciding on an action. To say 'we will think about it' after a decision has been made is a flaw.
ai.modern: ஒரு செயலைச் செய்வதற்கு முன் நன்றாகச் சிந்தித்து முடிவெடுக்க வேண்டும். முடிவெடுத்த பிறகு சிந்திப்போம் என்று நினைப்பது குற்றமாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the importance of thorough deliberation before committing to a course of action. The word 'eṇṇi' means having thought or considered, and 'tuṇika' urges a firm decision. Once a deed is resolved upon, second-guessing or delaying by saying 'we will think about it' is described as a flaw ('iḻukku'). The verse teaches that planning must precede action, and hesitation after a decision is detrimental.

ai.literal: In the proper way not striving effort, many people standing even if protected, flaw will incur.
ai.translation: An effort that is not exerted using the proper method will fail, even if many people stand together to protect it.
ai.modern: சரியான வழிமுறையில் முயற்சி செய்து தொடங்கப்படாத ஒரு செயல், பலரும் துணையாக நின்று காப்பாற்றினாலும் தோல்வியையே தழுவும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the importance of using the correct method for any undertaking. If an action is not performed with the proper approach, it is fundamentally unsound and bound to fail. Even if many people gather to support and protect the endeavor, their collective strength cannot save it. The word 'பொத்து' meaning a hole or flaw vividly illustrates how a poorly planned project will inevitably leak and collapse.

ai.literal: Good doing even in, fault there is, their respective nature having known not doing state.
ai.translation: Even in doing a good deed there is room for error, if it is done without understanding the nature of the people involved.
ai.modern: அவரவர் இயல்பை அறிந்து அதற்கேற்பச் செயல்படாவிட்டால், நன்மை செய்வதிலும் தவறு நேர்ந்துவிடும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns that good intentions alone are not enough when taking action. Even when performing a good deed, a fault can occur. This happens if one acts without first understanding the specific character and nature of the individuals involved. Careful consideration of the recipient is necessary to ensure that a good action yields a good result.

ai.literal: Not-despised [things] having considered doing is needed; with oneself not-agreeing [things] will not accept the world.
ai.translation: One must carefully consider and perform actions that will not be mocked. The world will not accept actions that do not befit one's own status.
ai.modern: உலகத்தார் பழித்துச் சிரிக்காத செயல்களை ஆராய்ந்து செய்ய வேண்டும். ஒருவருடைய தகுதிக்குப் பொருந்தாத செயல்களை உலகம் ஏற்றுக்கொள்ளாது.
ai.explanation: This couplet advises acting in a way that avoids public mockery and aligns with one's own capacity. The phrase 'eḷḷāta eṇṇi' means considering and choosing actions that others will not despise. The word 'tammōṭu' refers to oneself, and 'koḷḷāta' means things that do not fit or agree. If a person undertakes tasks that do not suit their own nature or status, the world ('ulaku') will not accept or respect them.
